name: Monastery and Site of the Escurial, Madrid
description: El Escorial is a vast granite complex about 45 km northwest of Madrid, built in the 1560s–80s for Philip II. It serves as monastery, royal palace, basilica, library and royal burial place all at once, and is often called the world's largest Renaissance building. Its severe, unadorned style shaped Spanish architecture for decades, and its layout is said to echo the grill on which St Lawrence was martyred.
